extractions.description: The paper proposes MOSAD (Multivariate Open-Set time-series Anomaly Detector), the first open-set time-series anomaly detection algorithm, combining a shared TCN feature extractor with Generative, Discriminative and Anomaly-Aware Contrastive heads, evaluated on SMD, PTB-XL and TUSZ against unsupervised and supervised baselines.

type.quote: Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets establish MOSAD as a new state-of-the-art in the TSAD field.
type.justification: Proposes a method and validates it with extensive experiments on three real-world datasets.

name.quote: Numerous methods for time-series anomaly detection (TSAD) have emerged in recent years
name.justification: The paper's main field of contribution.

name.quote: Recently, open-set anomaly detection (OSAD) methods are proposed to leverage a limited number of anomalous samples in the training phase
name.justification: The paper addresses open-set anomaly detection for time series.

name.quote: we verify MOSAD’s performance on both industrial and physiological signals
name.justification: ECG and EEG datasets used as evaluation venues.

name.quote: OSAD is different from the research fields of open-set recognition (OSR) [5] and out-of-distribution detection (OOD) [32].
OSAD is different from the research fields of open-set recognition (OSR) [5] and out-of-distribution detection (OOD) [32].
While open-set anomaly detection has witnessed significant advancements in computer vision, it remains unaddressed in the time-series domain.
name.justification: Referenced as a field where open-set AD has been studied.
